reason: H0 exercises the generic archive_read_open_memory/ archive_read_data_block path and includes 7-Zip BCJ/LZMA seeds, but it has no seed identified as BCJ2. S1 adds a distinct, stateful four-source BCJ2 decoding protocol involving one main stream, three buffered sub-streams, range-decoder state, repeated pack-stream seeking, allocation, and partial-output carryover. Sparse byte mutation of non-BCJ2 archives is not a reliable way to construct the tightly constrained BCJ2 folder topology required to reach this code, so the new BCJ2 attack surface is materially under-covered.
evidence: H0's 7-Zip corpus names include test_read_format_7zip_bcj_lzma1.7z and test_read_format_7zip_bcj_lzma2.7z, but none identifies _7Z_X86_BCJ2 or BCJ2.

setup_decode_folder only enters BCJ2 preparation when found_bcj2 is set and then requires specific structures: four packed streams and either numInStreams == 7 plus numOutStreams == 4, or numInStreams == 5 plus numOutStreams == 2.

setup_decode_folder reads and reallocates three sub-stream buffers, resets the reader to the main stream, and initializes main_stream_bytes_remaining, sub_stream_bytes_remaining, tmp_stream_bytes_remaining, and bcj2_outPos.
Bcj2_Decode consumes four coordinated sources and maintains bcj_state, bcj2_p, bcj2_range, bcj2_code, bcj2_prevByte, bcj2_outPos, and odd_bcj_size across calls.

H0 mutates fewer than 1% of bytes in fixed valid archives and only repeats archive_read_next_header/archive_read_data_block; it does not generate BCJ2 coder graphs, coordinated sub-stream sizes, truncated BCJ2 side streams, or output-boundary states.
recommended_action: Add a structure-aware 7-Zip BCJ2 fuzz target or valid BCJ2 seed corpus covering both setup_decode_folder stream_type forms, then mutate coder graphs, pack positions and sizes, all three side streams, the main stream, truncation points, and output boundaries while driving archive_read_next_header and archive_read_data_block through multiple calls and cleanup.
